p: Hunstanton is a seaside town with two very different sides, and a SEA LIFE visit fits neatly into either. New Hunstanton is the classic resort, with its green, promenade and amusements, while Old Hunstanton just up the coast is quieter, with dunes, beach huts and the old lighthouse standing on the cliff top. Walking between the two along the cliffs or the beach is a lovely way to spend an hour after the aquarium.

For the visit itself, plan on a couple of hours. Little ones love the rock pool style displays and the chance to see what lives in the water off their own beach, and the seal hospital side of things gives older children a real-world story to follow. If you can, time your visit around one of the feeding talks, as they're often the highlight.

There's plenty more nearby if you're staying a few days. The royal Sandringham Estate is a short drive inland, with woodland walks and a country park that's free to explore. Norfolk Lavender at Heacham is a colourful stop in summer, and bird lovers will want to head east to RSPB Titchwell Marsh, where the reserve paths run all the way to the beach.

Hunstanton's beach faces west across the Wash, which means sunsets over the water, something you don't get on the rest of the east coast. Grab some chips, find a bench on the front and watch the sky go orange. It's the perfect end to a day of seals and sea creatures.
Do keep an eye on the tide if you head out across the sands, as it comes in quickly on this flat stretch of coast.
